subject: Animation
title: Brenda Chapman: Breaking the Glass Ceiling
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Brenda Chapman: Breaking the Glass Ceiling.

hook.text: Brenda Chapman was the first woman to direct an animated feature at a major studio when she led Brave at Pixar.

buildup.text: Chapman had already co-directed The Prince of Egypt at DreamWorks, proving her leadership ability.

discovery.text: Brave told a story about a mother-daughter relationship — a theme Chapman drew from her own family life.

twist.text: Pixar replaced Chapman as director midway through production. Mark Andrews finished the film.

climax.text: Chapman shared the Oscar for Brave, but her removal highlighted the gender struggles women face in animation.

punchline.text: She won the Oscar for a film she was fired from directing.

quiz.question: Why was Brenda Chapman's work on Brave significant?
options: She invented the 3D rendering used in the film
She was the first woman to direct an animated feature at a major studio, despite being replaced mid-production
